blocks.content: The long polling topic reduced wasted requests, but still requires opening a brand new connection right after every single response, a real, remaining cost. Server sent events removes that specific cost entirely for a genuinely common case, when a server needs to keep pushing new information to a client repeatedly over time.

The core idea is a real, meaningful step forward: keep just ONE connection open, and let the server send as many events down it as it wants, whenever it actually wants, with no need to reopen anything in between.

1. The Key Improvement Over Long Polling
blocks.text: 1. The Key Improvement Over Long Polling

blocks.content: Long polling, exactly as covered in the previous topic, requires opening a brand new request right after every single response, real, repeated connection setup overhead. Server sent events instead keeps just ONE single connection open for as long as needed, letting the server send many separate events down that same connection over time, with zero repeated setup cost at all.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437869261-782477565.png
blocks.alt: The Key Improvement Over Long Polling

blocks.content: 2. A Genuinely One Directional Stream

Server sent events establishes a continuous stream flowing specifically FROM the server TOWARD the client. The client only ever receives events over this particular channel, it does not send data back to the server over this same connection at all, that direction genuinely does not exist here.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437869262-174042839.png

blocks.title: This one directional nature is a deliberate design choice
blocks.content: It is not a limitation that was simply overlooked, it is exactly what makes server sent events genuinely simple and lightweight for the specific, common case of a server needing to keep pushing updates, without needing the added complexity of handling data flowing the other way too.
3. A Simple, Lightweight Event Format

Each individual event sent down the stream uses a simple, lightweight text format, specifically designed to be easy for a browser to parse automatically, with built in browser support for consuming this exact format with minimal application code required.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437869262-678128634.png
4. Automatic Reconnection Built Right In

If the underlying connection drops unexpectedly, for any real network reason, the browser automatically attempts to reconnect on its own, with genuinely no extra application code required to handle this basic recovery case. This is a real, practical advantage baked directly into how browsers natively support this technology.

5. Real, Natural Use Cases

A live news or sports score feed, continuously pushing updates as they happen, is a natural fit. Real time notifications, alerting a user the moment something relevant occurs, fit just as well. A live progress or status update stream, showing a long running task advancing in real time, is another genuinely common, natural use case.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437869262-36380823.png

{"headers":["Use case","Why server sent events fits naturally"],"rows":[["Live score feed","Purely server to client updates, no data needs to flow back"],["Real time notifications","The client only ever needs to receive, never send, over this channel"]]}
6. The Real, Honest Limitation

Server sent events is genuinely one directional only, and this has to be stated plainly. An application that also needs the client to send meaningful data back to the server still needs a separate, ordinary HTTP request for that other direction entirely, server sent events was never built to handle that side of the conversation at all.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437870004-212793341.png
7. A Real World Analogy

A radio station broadcasting continuously captures this precisely. Listeners simply tune in and receive whatever the station sends, effortlessly and continuously, but they genuinely cannot talk back to the station over that exact same broadcast channel, that would require a completely separate communication path entirely.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437870006-807300799.png

blocks.title: A genuine forward pointer
blocks.content: When an application genuinely needs true two way, real time communication in both directions at once, the next topic in this module, websockets, is specifically built for exactly that case.
8. Common Mistakes and Key Takeaways

It is genuinely one directional, server to client only, a deliberate design choice, not an oversight.
Automatic reconnection and event parsing are handled natively by the browser, requiring minimal extra application code.
